iWhat this dashboard is & how leaders are picked▸
What you're looking at

Live open positions of the top polymarket.com traders we follow. Each row is an individual bet (combos don't exist on polymarket.com — see note). Click any market title to open the bet on polymarket.com, or the US↗ tag to search for an equivalent tradeable market on polymarket.us.

How we pick leaders

Traders are ranked on the overall-monthly-PnL leaderboard (/v2/leaderboard) and then gated on:

  • Win rate ≥ 55% on settled markets (not realized PnL alone)
  • Closed trades ≥ 20 so win-rate is statistically meaningful
  • ROI > 0 over the evaluated window

Those who pass become the follow-list. Their WR / ROI / T (total closed) are shown under each trader's name on the row.

The score (0–100) column

A composite to surface trades most worth copying. Each row shows 3 component chips (WR / SZ / PNL) under the total, so you can see why a score is high. Hover any chip for its range.

  • WR (0–40): trader's historical win rate. 60% WR = 13 pts, 70% = 27, 80%+ = 40. Below 50% = 0. Highest weight because track record is the best single predictor.
  • SZ (0–35): this bet's size as a multiple of the trader's typical. 1x = 12, 2x = 24, 5x+ = 35. Big-for-them bets = conviction signal.
  • PNL (0–25): position stage. 0 to +30% up = 25 (validated but still has room). −10 to 0 = 18 (early dip, maybe entry point). +30%+ = 5 (late runner, less upside).

Dropped from score (2026-11-25): "Price sweet spot" (0–15 for bets near $0.50). Opaque and diluted the WR/SZ signals. Say the word and I'll bring it back.

On combos / parlays

Every entry is an individual bet. Polymarket.com doesn't offer combo/parlay orders — that's a polymarket.us-only product. The closest signal here is BASKET markers on positions in a mutually exclusive outcome set (e.g., "who wins the nomination?"). Multiple legs of a basket from one trader is hedging within one event, not a parlay.

iHow to read this tab▸
  • Value — Polymarket sells an outcome at a different price than the sportsbooks. It's a prediction that the books are closer to the truth, not a sure thing. Paper record so far: 6–0.
  • Fair price — the reference's win chance with the bookmaker's cut removed, as a percentage and as American odds (−150: bet $150 to win $100; +130: bet $100 to win $130).
  • Edge is fair price minus Polymarket price, in percentage points (pp); positive means cheap on Polymarket. EV % is the average profit per $100 after fees if the fair price is right; small edges often turn negative after fees. Filter with Min edge and Sportsbook-priced only; click a header to sort.
  • Reference — DraftKings first (via ESPN), then the median of other US books (Book consensus). Only when no sportsbook has a line do we use our Record model, a simple formula of our own built from team records, flagged amber. Its edges run much larger and it is still being tested.
  • Paper bets — automatic $100 practice bets, no real money, on .us moneylines with EV of 2% or more and edge of 1.5pp or more, one per game. Status shows Paper bet open or Qualifies; the scoreboard at the bottom compares every paper strategy.

Value Polymarket vs sportsbooks

Venue:

.us — US exchange: NBA/NFL game moneylines + NBA player props, compared with DraftKings. .com — international exchange: soccer, college and other leagues we can match to DraftKings (only 11 NBA/NFL games listed there today).

iHow to read this tab▸
  • Structural arbitrage — Polymarket's own prices contradict each other, so buying the right combination pays out whatever happens. No prediction involved.
  • Neg-risk basket: several outcomes, exactly one wins; if all the YES prices add up to less than $1, one of each pays $1. Parity: YES + NO in one market costs less than $1. Ladder: "15+" priced above "10+", which can't both be right.
  • Fee buffer — a hit only counts if the profit after fees beats a 1% buffer for slippage.
  • Dust is a real gap too small to trade; Needs review means the gap depends on the outcome list being complete, so it isn't guaranteed.
